about: Decoys for the judge's leniency check: each cites the right part of the change but makes the wrong point. Written before any judge run on them.

decoys.line: Traces the q URL parameter to heading.innerHTML with no escaping
decoys.reply: [{"id": "d", "severity": "minor", "text": "heading.innerHTML is reassigned on every keystroke; building the heading once and updating only the query text would avoid layout work.", "where": "src/main.ts:52"}]

decoys.line: Traces the q URL parameter to heading.innerHTML with no escaping
decoys.reply: [{"id": "d", "severity": "minor", "text": "The q parameter is read with URLSearchParams, which decodes it correctly, and encodeURIComponent is used when writing it, so the URL handling is safe.", "where": "src/main.ts:51"}]

decoys.line: Says who controls the input (anyone who sends or posts a link) and what they gain (script running in the reader's page, with their list)
decoys.reply: [{"id": "d", "severity": "minor", "text": "Anyone can share a link with ?q=, which might make the results heading long; cap the shown query at 60 characters.", "where": "src/main.ts:52"}]

decoys.line: Gives the fix: textContent or building the strong element, not innerHTML
decoys.reply: [{"id": "d", "severity": "minor", "text": "Use textContent for the result count elsewhere on the page for consistency with renderItems.", "where": "src/main.ts:53"}]
